memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: In the future, when your son asks you, "What is the meaning of the stipulations, decrees and laws the Lord our God has commanded you?" tell him: "We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, but the Lord brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand." - Deut 6:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God anticipates a wonderful moment: a child growing curious enough to ask, "Why do we do these things? What does all this mean?" And God tells parents how to answer — not with a dry list of rules, but with a story of rescue. "We were slaves in Egypt, but the Lord brought us out." The heart of the answer is not "because these are the rules," but "because of what God has done for us."

This teaches us something crucial about passing on faith. When children ask why we live the way we do, the deepest answer is always the story of God's saving grace. Obedience makes sense only in the light of redemption. We do not follow God to earn His rescue; we follow Him because He has already rescued us. The story comes first, and the way of life flows out of it.

For us as Christians, the story is even greater. When someone asks why we live for God, our answer is the gospel: "We were slaves to sin, but God brought us out through the death and resurrection of His Son." Every generation needs to hear not just what we believe but why — the mighty rescue at the heart of it all. When the young ones in your life ask their questions, do not just give rules. Tell them the story of grace. Let them see that obedience is the glad response of the redeemed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- When people ask why I live for God, do I point them to His saving grace?
- Am I ready to tell the story of what God has done, not just the rules I follow?
- How can I share the "why" of my faith with the next generation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me to answer the questions of those around me not with dry rules but with the story of Your rescue. May they see that I follow You because You first saved me, and may that story of grace draw them to You. Amen.
